text:
olivia: Heads-up — after rotating a CMK in prod we started seeing AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt when services assume role 'svc/data-encryptor'. Anyone hit grant/token weirdness before?

nate: Did CloudTrail show the principal ARN in the KMS Decrypt event?

olivia: Pasted CloudTrail snippet:
```json
{
  "eventName": "Decrypt",
  "userIdentity": {"type": "AssumedRole", "arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/svc/data-encryptor/123"},
  "errorCode": "AccessDenied",
  "kmsKeyId": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345"
}
```

jordan: My first guess: key policy doesn't grant the assumed-role principal (only the base IAM role) or there's an EncryptionContext requirement. Check key policy principals and conditions.

lee: Also check if you relied on grants before rotation. Grants are tied to a key id and when you replace/rotate the key material or create a new CMK, grants can become invalid. Did you rotate by rekeying or by creating a brand-new key? Grants do not survive key replacement.

olivia: We rotated by creating a new CMK and updating the S3 re-encrypt job. We had created grants for the older key for the KMS proxy. Logs show an InvalidGrantToken right before AccessDenied:
```text
InvalidGrantToken: Grant token not recognized
at kms.amazonaws.com Decrypt
```

sec-bot: Two things to validate: 1) EncryptionContext mismatch — if Decrypt is called with an EncryptionContext and the key policy/condition requires it, a mismatch yields AccessDenied. 2) STS session policies / session tags — session policies attached at assume-role time can strip kms:Decrypt even if the role normally has it. Use the IAM policy simulator or examine the session policy in the AssumeRole call.

nate: Quick remediation checklist: (1) `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt` to gather events; (2) `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id>` to see active grants and `aws kms retire-grant --grant-id <id>` to clean stale tokens; (3) if you need immediate access, add the assumed-role ARN to the CMK key policy with explicit `kms:Decrypt` allow (temporary).

olivia: I'll try adding the role ARN to the key policy temporarily and revoke old grants. Will test and report back. Thanks :thumbsup:

jordan: If you need a short-term safety net, create a grant for the KMS proxy principal that includes `RetireGrant` so you can rotate keys without orphaning clients — and avoid relying on ephemeral grant tokens for long-lived workflows.

olivia: Will do. Posting results in ~30m.
